name: Composite monsoon scenario (synthetic)

model.name: HAND-threshold scenario

connectivity.note: REVIEW-04: the >=9-cell component-area filter replaces the 3x3 opening and is the only wet-mask component test; morphological opening is forbidden.

model.depth_bias: Conservative-shallow: a cell below the burnt channel datum reports the full stage, because no levee or bathymetry data exists to give it a deeper surface.

assumptions: Rainfall, main-stem stage, backwater allowance, stage values, step dates and the 2.0 m threshold are synthetic; no gauge record, official warning or predictive claim is represented. Stages are the phase-A curve rescaled by x1.48 (REVIEW-03 B1); the peak value is the calibration-selected 3.70 m.
The analysis domain is AOI v2: inside Assam and DEM <= 120 m, with a 2 km edge buffer used only for continuity. Flood/risk metrics count only AOI v2 core cells (REVIEW-02 A1).

Only OSM waterway=river is burned; ways are clipped to AOI v2 + 5 km, kept if their midpoint is inside that buffer and their clipped length is >= 2 km; only the Brahmaputra main stem is dilated to 2 cells (REVIEW-02 A2).
Stage is applied uniformly to every mapped channel; the water surface is flat within a step.

Inundation is a HAND threshold with a component-area filter; wet components smaller than 9 cells (0.073 km² at 90 m) are dropped before statistics, geometry and rendering (REVIEW-04 C2). The filter is an 8-connected component-area rule, not a morphological opening and not a separate channel-proximity test.
Depth is the bathtub convention depth = stage - max(HAND, 0), so depth <= stage; cells below the burnt datum report the full stage and are conservatively shallow (REVIEW-03 B2).

Depth-band frames are rendered as a 5-class paletted PNG at half the analysis resolution (about 180 m/px) plus frame-index.json; no per-band GeoJSON and no per-step vector outline are produced in M0 (REVIEW-04 C1).
The model is not calibrated to a gauge, satellite extent or event statistic.
The hydrograph is a declared synthetic shape: rainfall peaks at S04 and stage peaks at S07.
limitations: No hydrodynamic routing, unsteady flow, sediment transport or solved backwater term.
No levee, embankment, road or flood-defence failure is represented; protection is not subtracted.
The depth surface is conservative-shallow below the burnt datum: without levee or bathymetry data those cells cannot be assigned a deeper surface.
Mapped channels are incomplete, especially first-order streams; HAND is coarse near unmapped tributaries.
Analysis grid is 90 m; smaller channels, culverts and local depressions are not resolved.
Distances are Euclidean nearest-drainage distances, not flow-path lengths; a channel across a ridge can be selected.
No population, building, crop, casualty or asset-loss estimate is made; risk is scenario-conditional terrain risk, not expected loss.
